CausalChain: Chronic inflammation -> CAF activation -> ECM remodeling and stiffening -> Enhanced mechanotransduction + CAF-derived paracrine signaling -> YAP/TAZ pathway activation -> Recruitment of epigenetic modifiers (e.g., EZH2, HDACs) -> Epigenetic reprogramming -> Promotion of cancer stem cell traits -> Increased chemoresistance
Hypothesis: In cholangiocarcinoma, chronic inflammatory signals activate CAFs that remodel and stiffen the ECM. This mechanical alteration, complemented by a CAF secretome rich in cytokines and growth factors, induces mechanotransduction in tumor cells, leading to the activation of the YAP/TAZ signaling pathway. Activated YAP/TAZ then orchestrates the recruitment and/or activation of key epigenetic regulators—including specific histone methyltransferases and deacetylases such as EZH2 and HDACs—to enact changes in chromatin structure. These epigenetic modifications underpin the emergence of cancer stem cell traits and contribute to the development of chemoresistance. The integration of current technologies like 3D organoid models, atomic force microscopy for ECM stiffness, and single-cell epigenetic analyses will allow for precise dissection of this pathway, providing new therapeutic targets.
Abstract: Chronic inflammation in cholangiocarcinoma activates cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which remodel and stiffen the extracellular matrix (ECM). This biomechanical alteration, in conjunction with CAF-derived cytokine and growth factor signals, triggers tumor cell mechanotransduction leading to activation of the YAP/TAZ pathway. Activated YAP/TAZ subsequently recruits specific epigenetic modifiers, such as EZH2 and HDACs, to reprogram chromatin states. This epigenetic reprogramming promotes cancer stem cell traits and ultimately drives chemoresistance. We propose using advanced 3D culture systems, organoids integrated with real-time ECM stiffness measurement, and single-cell epigenomic profiling to delineate this multifaceted mechanism and identify novel therapeutic interventions.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis retains the original causal chain (chronic inflammation -> CAF activation -> ECM stiffening -> mechanotransduction -> YAP/TAZ activation -> epigenetic reprogramming -> cancer stemness and chemoresistance) but enhances it by incorporating paracrine signaling from CAFs, thereby acknowledging additional cytokine-mediated contributions. It also specifies potential epigenetic mediators (e.g., EZH2, HDACs) and introduces modern technological approaches (3D culture systems, atomic force microscopy, and single-cell epigenomics) to empirically test each step of the process, thus addressing gaps highlighted in the review while preserving the novelty and logical coherence of the original concept.
